questions.q: What is the minimum Java version required by Spring Boot 3?
o: Java 17
Java 8
Java 11
Java 21
questions.w: Spring Boot 3 is built on Spring Framework 6, which requires Java 17 or later. Java 21 is supported and adds virtual threads.

questions.q: What is the biggest source-level change when migrating from Spring Boot 2 to 3?
o: `javax.*` packages are renamed to `jakarta.*`
XML configuration becomes mandatory
Gradle replaces Maven as the build tool
All beans become prototype scoped
questions.w: Jakarta EE 9+ renamed the packages, so imports such as `javax.persistence` become `jakarta.persistence`. OpenRewrite recipes automate most of it.

questions.q: How do you turn on virtual threads for a Spring Boot 3.2+ web app on Java 21?
o: Set `spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true`
Add `@EnableVirtualThreads` to every controller
Replace Tomcat with Netty
Rewrite controllers to return `Mono`
questions.w: Blocking code keeps its simple style while the server handles requests on cheap virtual threads. Watch for pinning in `synchronized` blocks.

questions.q: What is Spring AOT used for?
o: Generating code and hints at build time for faster, native-ready startup
Making the unit tests run faster inside the CI pipeline
Compiling Java source code into JavaScript for browsers
Hot reloading changed classes inside a production server
questions.w: Ahead-of-time processing resolves bean definitions at build time. GraalVM native images need that because of the closed-world assumption.

questions.q: What does a GraalVM native image trade for its fast startup and low memory?
o: Longer builds, plus limits on reflection and dynamic features
Loss of support for ordinary Java classes and interfaces
Losing the ability to run on Linux container hosts
Giving up the use of Spring beans in the application
questions.w: Reflection, proxies and resources must be known at build time (hints). Peak throughput may also be lower than a warmed-up JIT JVM.

questions.q: Which class replaces `WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` in modern Spring Security?
o: A `SecurityFilterChain` bean
A `SecurityManager` subclass
An `@EnableOldSecurity` annotation
A `web.xml` file
questions.w: You now declare one or more `SecurityFilterChain` beans using the lambda DSL of `HttpSecurity`.

questions.q: What is the standard way to return errors in Spring 6 / Boot 3 REST APIs?
o: `ProblemDetail`, based on RFC 7807/9457 problem details
A plain string holding the stack trace
An HTML error page returned to every client
Always `200 OK` with an error field
questions.w: Enable with `spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled=true` or return `ProblemDetail` from an `@ExceptionHandler`.

questions.q: What does the Observation API in Spring 6 allow?
o: Instrumenting code once to get metrics, traces and log context
Watching files on disk and reloading them when they change
Observing user behaviour in the browser for analytics
Replacing the logging framework that the application uses
questions.w: It builds on Micrometer so one instrumentation point feeds Prometheus metrics and distributed tracing together.
